The database schema named 'rschema_0177' consists of three tables: Abstract_File, Directory, and File.
The Abstract_File table represents the abstract details of a file. It has five columns: Creation_Time (of type DATETIME), File_ID (of type INTEGER, acting as the primary key), Name (of type VARCHAR(255)), Type (of type VARCHAR(255)), and Update_Time (of type DATETIME).
The Directory table is linked to the Abstract_File table via the File_ID column, acting as a foreign key. It has two columns: Directory_ID (of type INTEGER, acting as the primary key) and Sub-file/directory_list (of type BLOB).
The File table is linked to both the Abstract_File and Directory tables via the Abstract_File_ID and Directory_ID columns, respectively, acting as foreign keys. It has seven columns: Abstract_File_ID (of type INTEGER, not null), Creation_Time (of type DATETIME), Directory_ID (of type INTEGER, not null), File_ID (of type INTEGER, acting as the primary key), File_Size (of type FLOAT), Name (of type VARCHAR(255)), Type (of type VARCHAR(255)), and Update_Time (of type DATETIME).
This schema ensures referential integrity by enforcing foreign key constraints. When a record in the Abstract_File table is deleted or updated, the corresponding records in the Directory and File tables will also be affected, as defined by the CASCADE delete or update rules.
gold_question:
In the File/Directory (AbstractFile) module, users can create files or directories. When creating, enter the file ID (FileID) as the Primary key to uniquely identify the file or directory; enter the name (Name) for easy identification; select the type (Type), which can only be a file or directory; the system automatically records the creation time (CreateTime) to save the creation time of the file or directory; the update time (UpdateTime) will be updated when the file or directory information is modified. Users can modify the name and type of the file or directory, and the system will update the update time accordingly.
In the Directory (Folder) module, when users create a directory, they enter the directory ID (FolderID) as the Primary key; associate the file ID (FileID) as the Foreign key to ensure that it is associated with the file or directory in the AbstractFile table; set the child file/directory list (ChildList) and add the ID of the child file or subdirectory to this list; users can add or delete child files/directories, and the system will update the child file/directory list and update the update time. Users can also modify the file ID of the directory, and the system will check the Foreign key association and update the update time.
In the File module, when creating a file, the user enters the file ID (FileID) as the Primary key; enters the name (Name) and selects the type (Type), limiting it to file; enters the file size (FileSize) to indicate the size of the file; the system will record the creation time (CreateTime) and update time (UpdateTime), and update the update time when the file information is modified. The user can modify the file name, type and file size, and the system will update the corresponding information and update the update time. "

-- Schema for database: rschema_0177
CREATE TABLE `abstract_file` (
  `creation_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `file_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `update_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`file_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `directory` (
  `directory_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `sub_file_directory_list` blob DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`directory_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `directory_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`directory_id`) REFERENCES `abstract_file` (`file_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `file` (
  `abstract_file_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `creation_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  `directory_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `file_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `file_size` float DEFAULT NULL,
  `name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `update_time` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`file_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `file_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`abstract_file_id`) REFERENCES `abstract_file` (`file_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `file_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`directory_id`) REFERENCES `directory` (`directory_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
